summary_paragraph: Mr. ___ , a man with secondary progressive multiple sclerosis and a history of recurrent urinary tract infections due to resistant organisms, was admitted after being found lethargic at home with high fever, chills, and weakness. He was diagnosed with severe sepsis secondary to an ESBL-producing E. coli infection originating from the urinary tract, with bacteremia and acute kidney injury. He responded well to fluid resuscitation and intravenous piperacillin-tazobactam, with normalization of lactate, kidney function, and clinical status. A PICC line was placed to complete a full course of IV antibiotics at a rehabilitation facility. His chronic left hip wound, sustained from a fall, was monitored but not considered infected. He was discharged to extended care with plans for wound care, antibiotic completion, and follow-up with his primary care and specialty providers.
